title: NYC map of impunity: buyer posts, named areas, enforcement and cases, 2020 to 2026
note: Compiled from a dataset brief supplied by CATW on 20 November 2026 and checked by the agent where the source could be read: the UNCO 2025 report (read page by page), the Queens DA, 1010 WINS, QNS and Queens Daily Eagle pages (read). The CATW 2022 report quotes are reproduced as the report prints them, with its redactions, and were not re-read by the agent (verified_by_agent false). Nothing here was collected from a buyer forum by this project. Pins are at neighbourhood level; no street address is stored. The forum layer ends in mid-2023; 2024 to 2026 is enforcement and case records only.

venues.text: Roosevelt Avenue. A trafficking indictment describes a woman brought from Mexico forced to earn $800 a night on the avenue (Queens DA, 2025). Advocates mapped 14 alleged brothels between 77th and 111th Streets (QNS, January 2025); the NYPD counted more than 20 court-ordered closures along the avenue in the previous 12 months.

cases.title: Somorie Moses: murder in the course of sex trafficking
cases.text: Indicted on 10 charges including sex trafficking and the January 2017 murder of Leondra Foster, beaten to death. Court documents say he pimped women from 2003. Believed to be the first use of the federal statute criminalizing murder in the course of sex trafficking. Leondra Foster is in the memorial on the New York page.

cases.title: Valezka Echeverrias: trafficking on Roosevelt Avenue
cases.text: Eleven-count indictment: three counts of sex trafficking, grand larceny, promoting prostitution. A woman brought from Mexico around November 2022 was forced to pay $800 a night from sex with men on Roosevelt Avenue; a second victim $100 a day in 2023. Prior indictment November 2024. Up to 25 years on the top count.

cases.title: Operation Restore Roosevelt
cases.text: A 90-day multi-agency action on the Roosevelt Avenue corridor: more than 2,500 arrests (Queens Eagle, Nov 2026) and more than 6,700 summonses; a dozen illegal sex shops and brothels closed since October (City Hall, Jan 2025). Advocates said the trade returned when it ended.
cases.source: QNS (8 Jan 2025); Queens Daily Eagle (2 Nov 2026)

cases.title: Jackson Heights brothel closed; 13 buyers arrested
cases.text: Police shuttered an alleged brothel on 75th Street on 28 October 2026. The next day 13 people were arrested for patronizing near Roosevelt Avenue and 87th Street.

cases.title: NYPD prostitution arrests, 2020
cases.text: 61.5% of people arrested in prostitution cases were buyers and 24% were people in prostitution; 96 people in prostitution arrested in 2020 against 1,790 in 2014; 246 patrons arrested. The page could not be read by the agent; figures as compiled in the brief.

cases.title: Bronx hotel and motel ring targeting teenage girls
cases.text: Six men arrested for a ring that reached teenage girls through social media. No reports of buyers being apprehended.

cases.title: Bronx child sex trafficking indictment
cases.text: A registered sex offender indicted for bringing girls as young as 12 to his apartment, 2018 to 2020: the first use of the Attorney General's Sex Trafficking of a Child charge. No reports of buyers apprehended.

cases.title: Flushing trafficking ring
cases.text: Nine traffickers arrested for a ring recruiting and exploiting Chinese women in hotels around the U.S.

cases.title: Borough prosecution policy shifts
cases.text: The Bronx DA dismissed hundreds of prostitution charges; the Brooklyn DA stopped prosecuting people in prostitution while keeping patronizing; the Manhattan DA ended prosecution of prostitution and unlicensed massage and dismissed thousands of loitering cases.

cases.title: John stings as overtime
cases.text: A retired officer describes john stings as overtime work; since 2014 the city paid over $1 million to at least 20 people claiming false arrest in prostitution or john stings, including $150,000 to five young Latino men. Not read by the agent; as compiled in the brief.
